title: GNU Make / Makefile analyzer (M60, 2026-09-27)
question: The website advertises a Make analyzer via SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES. Do we have one, and is it any good?
verdict: We had one: wired into engine.ts, advertised, and named by ZERO gates. Now gated, measured and rebuilt. 18 defects found and fixed. The most consequential finding is not among them: FOUR gates existed for this lane and none had been run — two of the eighteen defects and one dead branch were sitting inside checks that would have reported green. Recall/precision 1.000000; completeness A-H 8/8; all four M12 gates now execute.

sourceVsWasm.anonymousNote: 130 anonymous ids in the wasm vs 91 declared: node-types.json deduplicates identical anonymous tokens the id table lists once per id. Not part of the proof, and recorded rather than hidden.
sourceVsWasm.namedIdNote: 46 named IDS for 44 unique names (`word` and `text` each hold 2 ids) — which is why the inventory prints 46 against a 44-entry spec.

patches: P1 `_ordinary_rule`: target-scoped `target: export VAR = value` (closed MAKE-G3)
P2 `_shell_escape`: `$$( ... )` as a shell command, not a make expansion (closed MAKE-G4)
grammar.patchDecision: ADOPT. Both gaps were originally recorded as deliberately unpatched to protect the source<->wasm identity proof; that trade was then priced and does not hold, because the patches add NO node type and NO field (44 named / 24 fields before and after, zero added, zero removed) so the proof loses nothing and is re-measured for the patched source at 189 ids / 44 named / 131 anon / 24 fields, 0 missing, 0 extra. Measured 11 -> 0 ERROR nodes over the 99-file corpus with 0 files regressed, and at the PRODUCT level 1,772 -> 1,781 symbols / 5,870 -> 5,880 relationships, with all 19 lost facts being error-recovery garbage or a reference re-attributed to its correct owner. The analyzer required NO change, which is the strongest evidence the patch is well-founded. A control build of the unpatched source with the same toolchain is functionally identical to the pristine wired build, so every difference is the patch and not the toolchain.
grammar.retained: grammars/tree-sitter-make/ab/{pristine-grammar.js,grammar.patch,pristine-make.wasm} — the A/B stays re-runnable, not merely asserted.

corpus.rule: filenames in {Makefile, makefile, GNUmakefile, Makefile.am, Makefile.in} or suffix .mk; skipping .git, node_modules, vendor, target, dist, build, .venv, deps

differential.independence: the oracle derives names by a THIRD route (node text + delimiters, regex for assignments) and is two-phase with a per-frame owner; of the 5 rounds it took to reach 1.0, FOUR were oracle bugs and ONE was a real analyzer defect (the ${VAR} form), which is the argument for running it.

dangleAdjudication.note: only the operator-polluted class (112 edge ends) was a real defect; the rest are structural to GNU Make and are what the `uses` class exists for. 0 fell into a true-dangler bucket.

ruled.why: GNU Make has no type declaration, no base clause and no inheritance among its 44 named node types. The kind is not merely unused, it is INEXPRESSIBLE: there is no syntax from which
Same measurement as `extends`: Make has no interface to implement. A target that happens to satisfy a convention is a convention, not a declared type relationship, and reading one
The one kind with a REAL construct, and the ruling is measured rather than assumed. `override VAR = value` (2 occurrences) means this definition wins over a command-line or environ
Make has no `new` and no object construction. A recipe is a shell command that produces files; it is not an expression that yields a value, and nothing in the tree resembles a cons

complexity.linearity: no growth in per-node cost with file size: consistent with linear
complexity.withdrawnClaim: the first version bucketed by QUARTILES and printed a 1.208 'spread' with n=1 and n=0 buckets. 50 of 99 files sit within a few nodes of each other, so quartiles cannot work here; a spread over an empty bucket is not a measurement.

headline: line_number absent on 0 of 1,784 relationships (a product field; the address surfaces serve call-site positions from it) -> now 5,445/5,445
55 symbols carried their assignment operator (CGO_ENABLED?), which broke 112 edge ends BY CONSTRUCTION
references collected only from variable_assignment and rule, so a bare top-level $(foreach ... $(eval $(call ...))) produced zero edges
substitution_reference never read (a SIBLING of variable_reference, not a child) -> 9 corpus references lost
bare `export NAME` invisible (wraps a list, no assignment node anywhere)
computed includes dropped (`include $(shell ...)` is a shell_function node, not a function_call)
exports hardcoded [] -> a makefile's public surface unanswerable
imports sourced at a literal "makefile" -> two files including the same path produced the same edge
${VAR} (Make's second expansion form, 68 occurrences in 14 of 99 files) not normalised -> each fact published twice, one spelling dangling
define produced a constant, so a `calls` edge pointed at a value that cannot be called

D18: a rule whose TARGET is an EXPRESSION published no prerequisite edges at all — `$(BIN): $(OBJS) | builddir` declares no literal target, so the code iterated an empty list. 405 corpus edges lost. Found by the M12 contract probe, a gate that had existed for this lane and had never been run.
sharedHarness: the F5 file picker required a dotted extension, and Make's files are named `Makefile` — so the lane read as EMPTY rather than unchecked. Added an additive opt-in `fileNames` list; no other lane's matching changes.

the F5 label allowlist registered only 3 of the 6 labels the make oracle derives, so 1,500 analyzer edges were filtered off and reported as 1,498 MISSING (92% of truth) while the analyzer was emitting 2,109 edges for those 53 files.

three M12 gates hardcoded an `elixir` corpus that is not on this machine and died with `fatal: cannot change to ...` before measuring anything. The corpus now comes from script/m12/make-corpus.ts, a missing checkout is skipped and RECORDED, and both corpus gates pin the grammar residual instead of demanding zero errors.
defects.note_untested: Found by asking the census which declared types the corpus never fires, and then asking what the analyzer claims to do with THOSE. A `case` label is a claim, not a test. See reviews/make/master-review.md section 12.

survivingMutantsFoundAndFixed: make/accept-keywords-as-names SURVIVED the first run: the fixtures had no forbid on the `export` keyword, so a mutant resurrecting 6 bad edges changed nothing. A surviving mutant is a hole in the suite, not a pass.

make/ignore-brace-expansion-form also survived: the fix normalises the target during EXTRACTION, so a result-level transform finds no ${...} to rewrite and the revert is a silent no-op. Rewritten to take the source and re-wrap only edges whose own line really contains the brace form.

gates.grammar pin: make registered; 0 drift; source<->wasm exact 0/0 both directions
gates.zero-unknown census: 0 unknown / 0 empty / 0 bad ranges / 0 ownerless / 0 symbol-free; 5,880/5,880 line_number; 0 files with ERROR/MISSING
gates.M12 corpus errors: passed — 14/14 clean, 0 crashes, 0 error nodes, grammar residual PINNED TO ZERO
gates.M12 corpus errors (residual pin behaviou: the two M12 corpus pins went RED when the patched grammar took the residual from 2 files / 9 nodes to 0. A pin that fails on an improvement rather than being edited to match one is the behaviour worth keeping, and the pre-patch values are recorded in both gates and in fixtures/make/out/grammar-ab.json.
gates.grammar A/B (99 files): pristine 188 ids / 44 named / 24 fields, 6 error files, 11 error nodes; patched 189 ids / 44 named / 24 fields, 5 error files, 0 error nodes. 3 files improved, 0 regressed. Note the 6->5 in 'error files' is NOT an improvement claim: the remaining 5 are files whose rootNode.hasError is set by a hidden recovery token with zero traversable ERROR or MISSING nodes, which engine.ts:1264 reports generically and the corpus gates classify separately.
gates.F3 fixtures: 7/7 — the 7th (make/directive-flags) covers five constructs that previously had a code path and no test
gates.F4 mutants: 21/21 caught — 3 added, one per defect found by that fixture, including one that REPRODUCES the pre-fix output rather than reverting a line, because after the fix the defective relationship no longer exists to mutate
gates.completeness: 44/44 classified (32 handled, 10 correctly silent), sections A-H 8/8 — and the bucket RULE was amended after five types were found sitting in handled_verified with neither a fixture nor a corpus occurrence
gates.never-fired audit: The census's `never fired` list is the highest-signal line in the lane and was being read as a coverage percentage. Cross-referencing it against what the analyzer claims to handle found 5 types with a code path and ZERO tests (private/override/undefine/unexport/shell_assignment, all at 0 of 99 corpus occurrences) and 1 that produced nothing (vpath_directive). Three of those paths were BROKEN: the one-line `private VAR = v` / `override VAR := v` spelling lost its flag because the walker reads the directive before the nested assignment; `undefine VAR` was an UNREACHABLE branch because its operand is a bare word in the `variable` field with no named children, so the child search could never match; and `unexport` cleared the metadata flag while leaving the `exports` edge, so the symbol table and the graph disagreed. All fixed, all pinned. Real corpus fact corrected: `override CFLAGS += ...` at tree-sitter-lua/Makefile:25 now records isOverride. Corpus counts are UNCHANGED (1781/5880) because none of these constructs appear in the corpus except that one annotation.

gaps.summary: `VPATH = src` is a declared node type the analyzer does not model, so the search path is not recorded. 0 occurrences across all 99 corpus files, so there is no evidence to design against and no regression to guard. The s

`.RECIPEPREFIX = >` changes what a recipe line looks like, so ignoring it means recipe lines using a non-default prefix are not recognized as recipes. 0 occurrences in this corpus (every one of the 99 files uses a tab),

Both grammar limitations fixed by two measured patches to the vendored grammar, which add no node type and no field. 11 -> 0 ERROR nodes over the 99-file corpus; 9 previously invisible declarations are now visible; the error-recovery artefacts the recovery had published as facts (a `?` as a variable name, a whole `VAR=value` as a name) are gone. The analyzer needed no change. The pristine build and the patch are retained under grammars/tree-sitter-make/ab/ so the comparison is re-runnable. See reviews/make/master-review.md section 11.

notClaimed: any absolute performance budget: the box ran at load 49-50 throughout with nine agents on it, so every timing here is relative with the load recorded
any weight behind `calls`: it rests on ONE corpus site, and the count says so
notClosed.summary: Only MAKE-G1 and MAKE-G2 remain open, and both are corpus-COVERAGE gaps rather than correctness defects: 0 occurrences in 99 files means there is no evidence to design against and no regression to guard. The two grammar gaps that were open are closed and the corpus ERROR residual is pinned to zero.

incidents: the hcl LANG_CONFIGS entry was NEVER COMMITTED — it lived only in a dirty worktree and a concurrent `git checkout` deleted it, after which `--lang hcl` threw `unknown language hcl`. Restored here and marked as a restoration; the gate itself then caught my reconstruction being wrong (I had required `calls`, which hcl rules N/A), so the restored entry is verified rather than assumed.

`script/**` is NOT in the typecheck program (root tsconfig includes `src/**/*.ts` only), so `npx tsc --noEmit` never sees the harnesses. I reported a shared file as type-clean on that basis while it had a syntax error. `bun build <file> --target=bun` is the real syntax gate for script/**.
`open(p,'wb')` truncates BEFORE the write fails: a full disk turned one mutant insertion into an empty mutate-analyzer.ts. All writes in this lane go temp-file + os.replace, verified after each.

the analyzer carried ONE regex literal I introduced (a `String.split` on a two-character pattern in moduleName), found by the M12 contract probe's zero-regex check. Fixing it then tripped the same check again, because my explanatory comment quoted the old expression and the detector only exempts `//` comments — a regex quoted in a doc comment reads to the next maintainer as a regex in the file.
the analyzer had a dead `endif_directive` branch: the grammar declares no such node type, so it could never run and read as coverage. Found by the node-types gate, and removed.

torrentinim/Makefile reports hasError=true with ZERO ERROR and ZERO MISSING nodes — the engine's generic hidden-recovery-token warning (engine.ts:1264). It parses into the correct tree and the analyzer's output for it is correct. Counting it as a file error would have hidden the two REAL grammar gaps behind a third phantom, so the two classes are now separated and pinned separately.
